name: Jachin
overview: Jachin was a male Levite who served as the twenty-first chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in Israel. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the sons of Aaron, which placed him within a significant priestly lineage. His role as a priest highlights his importance in the religious organization of ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jachin means 'he establishes,' reflecting a meaning rooted in stability or foundation. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 24:17 and was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Jachin is identified as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to a prominent priestly family within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this connection, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him apart from what is noted in his priestly lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Jachin's significance lies in his role within the structured priestly courses that organized Israel's worship and temple service. Being the twenty-first priestly course in the line of Eleazar underscores his part in maintaining the continuity of priestly duties ordained by God. His inclusion in the biblical record emphasizes the careful order God established for the service of the tabernacle and later the temple.
